draft.title: The Big Bang and expansion
card: The Big Bang model says the universe began extremely hot and dense, and space has been expanding ever since. It describes the expansion of space itself, not an explosion into empty space.
Light from distant galaxies has longer wavelengths than expected, shifted towards the red end of the spectrum. This fits galaxies moving away from us as space expands.
The cosmic microwave background (CMB) is faint microwave radiation coming from every direction in the sky. It is left over from the early hot universe, and it has cooled as space expanded.
Both observations support the model. The red shift shows the universe is expanding now, and the CMB is a relic of the hot early stage.
draft.remember: The universe began hot and dense and has expanded since, backed by red-shifted galaxies and the CMB.

a.q: Astronomers find that light from most distant galaxies is red-shifted. What does this observation support?
opts: Space is filled with microwave radiation
a.why: Longer wavelengths fit galaxies moving away as space expands. The microwave radiation is a separate observation, the CMB, and a red shift does not show it.
a.clue: Red shift means the wavelength has grown longer.

b.q: A student says the CMB is evidence for the Big Bang. Which reason best supports this?
opts: It is radiation left from the hot early universe
It shows galaxies are moving away from us
It comes from stars in our own galaxy only
It shows the universe began as an explosion in space
b.why: The CMB is a relic of the hot, dense early universe, now cooled to microwaves. The idea that galaxies move away is the red shift evidence. The Big Bang is the expansion of space, not an explosion into space.
b.clue: Think about what the CMB is left over from.

b.best: It is radiation left from the hot early universe
